EST. 2026 / V0.1
The screen is a living surface.

Nullworx is an experimental library of procedural effects for developers and creative coders. Fields of characters, masks with a pulse, and materials that behave less like decoration and more like weather.

01 / PREMISE

A SMALL LIBRARY WITH A HIGH BAR
Designed to behave like matter.

Most component libraries give you a finished surface. Nullworx starts with a behaviour: a field that reads a video, a mask that keeps its grain, a wave that reacts to a pointer. The reusable part is the system underneath.

READ THE LAB NOTES
→
A
The effect is the interface.

A live field should earn its place on the page. No hero image pretending to be software.

B
Source is part of the design.

Readable TypeScript, colocated styles, no hidden runtime. Copy it, keep it, change it.

C
A release is a decision, not a build.

Compiling is not publishing. Art, provenance, accessibility and the owner all have to agree.

02 / TERRITORY

FOUR AREAS / ONE RELEASE GATE
Four ways of unsettling a rectangle.

These are territories, not promises. Research means the lab is exploring the behaviour; it does not mean a download is waiting. The public catalogue stays empty until an effect passes review.

01
Character fields

Video, chance and time rebuilt as whole characters. ASCII waves, terminal rain and animated glyph systems.

ONE STUDY IN REVIEW
ASCII
WebGL
Glyphs
02
Living stencils

Masks that keep the grain of their material. Cell mosaics, SVG cut-outs and alpha fields that react.

RESEARCH
SVG
Alpha
Masks
03
Botanical systems

Flowers and growth structures generated from rules rather than drawn frame by frame.

RESEARCH
Generative
Motion
04
Visual materials

Light, ink, caustics and noise treated as substances with weight, not as background dressing.

RESEARCH
Materials
Shaders

The catalogue opens one gate at a time.

An effect is only public when it has cleared art review, provenance, licensing, accessibility and a production check. A status here is not a marketing count. It is the actual state of the work.

UNRELEASED LAB PREVIEW This is an owner-review page, not a public release. It is noindexed, excluded from the sitemap and absent from the public catalogue. Release gate ↗ All lab previews ↗ NULLWORX / LAB / ASCII WAVES OWNER REVIEW / NWX-ASCII-WAVES ASCII Waves FLOWER FIELD OWNER REVIEW The build exists, but the owner has not approved the art for release. A video is sampled cell by cell, translated into a living field of characters, and pushed through a slow wave of light. REACT 19 / NEXT.JS 16 / WEBGL 2 MIT CODE CC0 1.0 MEDIA UPDATED 2026-10-28 01 / MATERIAL Live field INSTRUMENTED PREVIEW FALLBACK / POSTER FALLBACK RESET ASCII Waves could not start WebGL 2. WebGL 2 is unavailable in this browser. NWX / FIELD 001 MOTION / WAITING REDUCED MOTION FREEZES THE FIELD AUTOMATICALLY. MATERIAL CONTROLS ⧉ COPY CONFIG CELL PITCH Auto / 12–16 12 px 16 px 20 px ⌄ QUALITY High / DPR 2 Balanced / DPR 1.5 Efficient / DPR 1 ⌄ WAVE SPEED 1.0 MOTION POINTER EDDY Changes are live. Motion off freezes the wave clock, video frame and pointer response together. 02 / PARAMETERS What can be tuned DEFAULTS ARE REVIEWED VALUES PARAMETER DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR cellSize CELL PITCH auto Character size in CSS pixels. Auto chooses 12, 14 or 16 by container width. speed WAVE SPEED 1 Multiplier for the slow domain-warp clock. The default is the reviewed Flower timing. quality QUALITY high Caps render resolution against the browser's device-pixel ratio. High matches the reviewed Proof 03 default (device DPR, capped at 2). playing MOTION true Pause freezes the video frame, the wave clock and pointer response together. pointerInteraction POINTER EDDY true Lets the pointer disturb nearby sampling cells. Disabled under reduced motion. 03 / TECHNICAL How it behaves ONE RENDERER / ONE DRAW CALL One WebGL 2 fragment shader samples an muxed video texture on a monospaced character grid. Rec.601 luma selects from the ordered glyph ramp ` .:-+*=%@#`; the video's RGB feeds the ink. Sampling UVs are warped by a low-frequency noise and wave function. A native-resolution glyph atlas keeps punctuation crisp at each device-pixel ratio. The React wrapper owns lifecycle, responsive cell measurement, visibility pausing, pointer input, reduced-motion freezing, context-loss recovery and a poster fallback. REQUIREMENTS React 19 (the component uses React 18-compatible APIs). A browser with WebGL 2 and H.264 video decoding. A parent element with an explicit height or aspect ratio. The CC0 Flower MP4 and poster served from /media, or custom src and fallbackImage URLs. ACCESSIBILITY This is a decorative field, not a control. All essential page content remains available as text outside the canvas, and motion is optional. Reduced motion: With reduced motion enabled, the wave clock and video pause and pointer interaction is disabled. The field remains as a still image. 04 / SOURCE Use it REVIEW-ONLY PACKAGE REVIEW ARTIFACT / NOT A RELEASE This archive is kept for owner evaluation. It is not a Nullworx release; do not present it as one until the owner records approval. DOWNLOAD REVIEW BUNDLE ↓ INSTALL.SH ⧉ COPY COMMAND # Download the archive from this page, then: unzip ascii-waves-0.1.0.zip -d . The bundle preserves the reviewed five-file component layout and the CC0 media. FIELD.TSX ⧉ COPY USAGE "use client"; import { AsciiWaves } from "@/components/effects/ascii-waves/ascii-waves"; export function Field() { return (
); } The component fills its parent. Give that parent an explicit height or aspect ratio. 05 / PERFORMANCE Measured, with caveats SOURCE-REVIEW NUMBERS The reviewed WebGL 2 path draws one fullscreen quad per frame and samples one live video texture. It pauses offscreen and when the page is hidden. DESKTOP 65.2 fps 1440 × 900, DPR 2, RTX 4060, one draw call, 90 × 57 cell grid, 2.9% CPU task time. MOBILE VIEWPORT 138.0 fps 390 × 844, DPR 2, RTX 4060 host, 33 × 71 cell grid, 4.7% CPU task time. VIDEO UPLOADS ~29/s Measured in the source integration review; the live texture is only marked dirty when a frame is available. These are source-review measurements on a host with external GPU load, not a hardware guarantee or a fresh Nullworx benchmark. The field still depends on WebGL 2, video decode and the device GPU. The poster fallback is used when either fails. 06 / LICENCE What you may do CODE AND MEDIA ARE SEPARATE CODE MIT The Nullworx site and effect code are offered under the repository's MIT license. The Flower video and poster are CC0 1.0 from the MDN sample media. The component itself does not bundle fonts; it draws from the system monospace stack. MEDIA CC0 1.0 Flower media from the MDN sample library. Attribution is retained; the CC0 terms do not require it. https://opensource.org/license/mit ↗ https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ ↗ 07 / PROVENANCE Where this came from HASHES, NOT VIBES The source was carried from the UI Forge Flower integration. The shader, glyph atlas and Flower preset were preserved rather than rewritten. The original experiments remain untouched. EFFECT SOURCE TREE SHA-256 0eeaf099c210b601664398519d92d1201506ced1c293cd802e3891958f2200a1 UPSTREAM GIT HEAD 906f859db0125965cba71c51da1707c0a4c6d045 CAPTURED 2026-10-28 FILE HASHES (7) BROWSE THE SOURCE REPOSITORY ↗ HASH MANIFEST IS VALIDATED ON EVERY BUILD. RELEASE STATUS OWNER REVIEW · Owner release approval recorded Open · Source and media provenance hashed Prepared · Code and asset licenses verified Prepared · Reduced-motion and fallback behaviour verified Prepared · Production build and browser smoke tests pass Prepared No public catalogue entry exists. The only page is this unlisted lab preview. SEE THE RELEASE GATE ↗ AT A GLANCE EFFECT ID nwx-ascii-waves VERSION 0.1.0 CATEGORIES Glyph systems, Video fields FRAMEWORKS React 19, Next.js 16, WebGL 2 RELEASED Not yet UPDATED 2026-10-28 PUBLIC URL Not assigned NULLWORX DROPS Hear when the next effect clears the gate. Free, optional, double opt-in. SUBSCRIBE TO THE LETTER → BEFORE YOU COPY Source is a responsibility, not a flex. The bundle preserves the reviewed five-file component layout and the CC0 media. The reviewed usage mutes the video and the component defaults to muted playback. Keep `muted` set unless you provide your own user-initiated audio path. Set an explicit parent height. A zero-height parent produces a zero-height field. Distribution remains gated: this archive is a review artifact until the effect is RELEASED. 09 / NULLWORX DROPS Hear when the gate opens. Drops is a low-frequency note when an effect is released, with the source decisions, performance notes and the occasional free extra behind it. One address, two separate choices, no account. FREE NEWSLETTER CONSENT IS REQUIRED. FUTURE PREMIUM ANNOUNCEMENTS AND OFFERS ARE A SEPARATE UNCHECKED OPT-IN AND ARE NEVER IMPLIED BY DROPS. 01 / PREMISE

A SMALL LIBRARY WITH A HIGH BAR
Designed to behave like matter.

Most component libraries give you a finished surface. Nullworx starts with a behaviour: a field that reads a video, a mask that keeps its grain, a wave that reacts to a pointer. The reusable part is the system underneath.

READ THE LAB NOTES
→
A
The effect is the interface.

A live field should earn its place on the page. No hero image pretending to be software.

B
Source is part of the design.

Readable TypeScript, colocated styles, no hidden runtime. Copy it, keep it, change it.

C
A release is a decision, not a build.

Compiling is not publishing. Art, provenance, accessibility and the owner all have to agree.

02 / TERRITORY

FOUR AREAS / ONE RELEASE GATE
Four ways of unsettling a rectangle.

These are territories, not promises. Research means the lab is exploring the behaviour; it does not mean a download is waiting. The public catalogue stays empty until an effect passes review.

01
Character fields

Video, chance and time rebuilt as whole characters. ASCII waves, terminal rain and animated glyph systems.

ONE STUDY IN REVIEW
ASCII
WebGL

Living stencils

Masks that keep the grain of their material. Cell mosaics, SVG cut-outs and alpha fields that react.

RESEARCH

03
Botanical systems

Flowers and growth structures generated from rules rather than drawn frame by frame.

RESEARCH
Generative
Motion
04
Visual materials

Light, ink, caustics and noise treated as substances with weight, not as background dressing.

RESEARCH
Materials
Shaders

An effect is only public when it has cleared art review, provenance, licensing, accessibility and a production check. A status here is not a marketing count. It is the actual state of the work.

Release gate ↗ All lab previews ↗ NULLWORX / LAB / ASCII WAVES OWNER REVIEW / NWX-ASCII-WAVES ASCII Waves FLOWER FIELD OWNER REVIEW The build exists, but the owner has not approved the art for release. A video is sampled cell by cell, translated into a living field of characters, and pushed through a slow wave of light. REACT 19 / NEXT.JS 16 / WEBGL 2 MIT CODE CC0 1.0 MEDIA UPDATED 2026-10-28 01 / MATERIAL Live field INSTRUMENTED PREVIEW FALLBACK / POSTER FALLBACK RESET ASCII Waves could not start WebGL 2. WebGL 2 is unavailable in this browser. NWX / FIELD 001 MOTION / WAITING REDUCED MOTION FREEZES THE FIELD AUTOMATICALLY. MATERIAL CONTROLS ⧉ COPY CONFIG CELL PITCH Auto / 12–16 12 px 16 px 20 px ⌄ QUALITY High / DPR 2 Balanced / DPR 1.5 Efficient / DPR 1 ⌄ WAVE SPEED 1.0 MOTION POINTER EDDY Changes are live. Motion off freezes the wave clock, video frame and pointer response together. 02 / PARAMETERS What can be tuned DEFAULTS ARE REVIEWED VALUES PARAMETER DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR cellSize CELL PITCH auto Character size in CSS pixels. Auto chooses 12, 14 or 16 by container width. speed WAVE SPEED 1 Multiplier for the slow domain-warp clock. The default is the reviewed Flower timing. quality QUALITY high Caps render resolution against the browser's device-pixel ratio. High matches the reviewed Proof 03 default (device DPR, capped at 2). playing MOTION true Pause freezes the video frame, the wave clock and pointer response together. pointerInteraction POINTER EDDY true Lets the pointer disturb nearby sampling cells. Disabled under reduced motion. 03 / TECHNICAL How it behaves ONE RENDERER / ONE DRAW CALL One WebGL 2 fragment shader samples an muxed video texture on a monospaced character grid. Rec.601 luma selects from the ordered glyph ramp ` .:-+*=%@#`; the video's RGB feeds the ink. Sampling UVs are warped by a low-frequency noise and wave function. A native-resolution glyph atlas keeps punctuation crisp at each device-pixel ratio. The React wrapper owns lifecycle, responsive cell measurement, visibility pausing, pointer input, reduced-motion freezing, context-loss recovery and a poster fallback. REQUIREMENTS React 19 (the component uses React 18-compatible APIs). A browser with WebGL 2 and H.264 video decoding. A parent element with an explicit height or aspect ratio. The CC0 Flower MP4 and poster served from /media, or custom src and fallbackImage URLs. ACCESSIBILITY This is a decorative field, not a control. All essential page content remains available as text outside the canvas, and motion is optional. Reduced motion: With reduced motion enabled, the wave clock and video pause and pointer interaction is disabled. The field remains as a still image. 04 / SOURCE Use it REVIEW-ONLY PACKAGE REVIEW ARTIFACT / NOT A RELEASE This archive is kept for owner evaluation. It is not a Nullworx release; do not present it as one until the owner records approval. ); } The component fills its parent. Give that parent an explicit height or aspect ratio. 05 / PERFORMANCE Measured, with caveats SOURCE-REVIEW NUMBERS The reviewed WebGL 2 path draws one fullscreen quad per frame and samples one live video texture. It pauses offscreen and when the page is hidden. DESKTOP 65.2 fps 1440 × 900, DPR 2, RTX 4060, one draw call, 90 × 57 cell grid, 2.9% CPU task time. MOBILE VIEWPORT 138.0 fps 390 × 844, DPR 2, RTX 4060 host, 33 × 71 cell grid, 4.7% CPU task time. VIDEO UPLOADS ~29/s Measured in the source integration review; the live texture is only marked dirty when a frame is available. These are source-review measurements on a host with external GPU load, not a hardware guarantee or a fresh Nullworx benchmark. The field still depends on WebGL 2, video decode and the device GPU. The poster fallback is used when either fails. 06 / LICENCE What you may do CODE AND MEDIA ARE SEPARATE CODE MIT The Nullworx site and effect code are offered under the repository's MIT license. The Flower video and poster are CC0 1.0 from the MDN sample media. The component itself does not bundle fonts; it draws from the system monospace stack. MEDIA CC0 1.0 Flower media from the MDN sample library. Attribution is retained; the CC0 terms do not require it. https://opensource.org/license/mit ↗ https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ ↗ 07 / PROVENANCE Where this came from HASHES, NOT VIBES The source was carried from the UI Forge Flower integration. The shader, glyph atlas and Flower preset were preserved rather than rewritten. The original experiments remain untouched. 01 / PREMISE

A SMALL LIBRARY WITH A HIGH BAR
Designed to behave like matter.

Most component libraries give you a finished surface. Nullworx starts with a behaviour: a field that reads a video, a mask that keeps its grain, a wave that reacts to a pointer. The reusable part is the system underneath.

READ THE LAB NOTES
→
A
The effect is the interface.

A live field should earn its place on the page. No hero image pretending to be software.

B
Source is part of the design.

Readable TypeScript, colocated styles, no hidden runtime. Copy it, keep it, change it.

C
A release is a decision, not a build.

Compiling is not publishing. Art, provenance, accessibility and the owner all have to agree.

02 / TERRITORY

FOUR AREAS / ONE RELEASE GATE
Four ways of unsettling a rectangle.

These are territories, not promises. Research means the lab is exploring the behaviour; it does not mean a download is waiting. The public catalogue stays empty until an effect passes review.

01

Video, chance and time rebuilt as whole characters. ASCII waves, terminal rain and animated glyph systems.

UNRELEASED LAB PREVIEW This is an owner-review page, not a public release. It is noindexed, excluded from the sitemap and absent from the public catalogue. Release gate ↗ All lab previews ↗ NULLWORX / LAB / ASCII WAVES OWNER REVIEW / NWX-ASCII-WAVES ASCII Waves FLOWER FIELD OWNER REVIEW The build exists, but the owner has not approved the art for release. A video is sampled cell by cell, translated into a living field of characters, and pushed through a slow wave of light. REACT 19 / NEXT.JS 16 / WEBGL 2 MIT CODE CC0 1.0 MEDIA UPDATED 2026-10-28 01 / MATERIAL Live field INSTRUMENTED PREVIEW AUTOPLAY BLOCKED START REQUIRED RESET Autoplay did not start. Press Start live field to begin playback. NWX / FIELD 001 AUTOPLAY / BLOCKED REDUCED MOTION FREEZES THE FIELD AUTOMATICALLY. MATERIAL CONTROLS ⧉ COPY CONFIG CELL PITCH Auto / 12–16 12 px 16 px 20 px ⌄ QUALITY High / DPR 2 Balanced / DPR 1.5 Efficient / DPR 1 ⌄ WAVE SPEED 1.0 MOTION POINTER EDDY Changes are live. Motion off freezes the wave clock, video frame and pointer response together. 02 / PARAMETERS What can be tuned DEFAULTS ARE REVIEWED VALUES PARAMETER DEFAULT BEHAVIOUR cellSize CELL PITCH auto Character size in CSS pixels. Auto chooses 12, 14 or 16 by container width. speed WAVE SPEED 1 Multiplier for the slow domain-warp clock. The default is the reviewed Flower timing. quality QUALITY high Caps render resolution against the browser's device-pixel ratio. High matches the reviewed Proof 03 default (device DPR, capped at 2). playing MOTION true Pause freezes the video frame, the wave clock and pointer response together. pointerInteraction POINTER EDDY true Lets the pointer disturb nearby sampling cells. Disabled under reduced motion. 03 / TECHNICAL How it behaves ONE RENDERER / ONE DRAW CALL One WebGL 2 fragment shader samples an muxed video texture on a monospaced character grid. Rec.601 luma selects from the ordered glyph ramp ` .:-+*=%@#`; the video's RGB feeds the ink. Sampling UVs are warped by a low-frequency noise and wave function. A native-resolution glyph atlas keeps punctuation crisp at each device-pixel ratio. The React wrapper owns lifecycle, responsive cell measurement, visibility pausing, pointer input, reduced-motion freezing, context-loss recovery and a poster fallback. REQUIREMENTS React 19 (the component uses React 18-compatible APIs). A browser with WebGL 2 and H.264 video decoding. A parent element with an explicit height or aspect ratio. The CC0 Flower MP4 and poster served from /media, or custom src and fallbackImage URLs. ACCESSIBILITY This is a decorative field, not a control. All essential page content remains available as text outside the canvas, and motion is optional. Reduced motion: With reduced motion enabled, the wave clock and video pause and pointer interaction is disabled. The field remains as a still image. 04 / SOURCE Use it REVIEW-ONLY PACKAGE REVIEW ARTIFACT / NOT A RELEASE This archive is kept for owner evaluation. It is not a Nullworx release; do not present it as one until the owner records approval. DOWNLOAD REVIEW BUNDLE ↓ INSTALL.SH ⧉ COPY COMMAND # Download the archive from this page, then: unzip ascii-waves-0.1.0.zip -d . The bundle preserves the reviewed five-file component layout and the CC0 media. FIELD.TSX ⧉ COPY USAGE "use client"; import { AsciiWaves } from "@/components/effects/ascii-waves/ascii-waves"; export function Field() { return (
); } The component fills its parent. Give that parent an explicit height or aspect ratio. 05 / PERFORMANCE Measured, with caveats SOURCE-REVIEW NUMBERS The reviewed WebGL 2 path draws one fullscreen quad per frame and samples one live video texture. It pauses offscreen and when the page is hidden. DESKTOP 65.2 fps 1440 × 900, DPR 2, RTX 4060, one draw call, 90 × 57 cell grid, 2.9% CPU task time. MOBILE VIEWPORT 138.0 fps 390 × 844, DPR 2, RTX 4060 host, 33 × 71 cell grid, 4.7% CPU task time. VIDEO UPLOADS ~29/s Measured in the source integration review; the live texture is only marked dirty when a frame is available. These are source-review measurements on a host with external GPU load, not a hardware guarantee or a fresh Nullworx benchmark. The field still depends on WebGL 2, video decode and the device GPU. The poster fallback is used when either fails. 06 / LICENCE What you may do CODE AND MEDIA ARE SEPARATE CODE MIT The Nullworx site and effect code are offered under the repository's MIT license. The Flower video and poster are CC0 1.0 from the MDN sample media. The component itself does not bundle fonts; it draws from the system monospace stack. MEDIA CC0 1.0 Flower media from the MDN sample library. Attribution is retained; the CC0 terms do not require it. https://opensource.org/license/mit ↗ https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ ↗ 07 / PROVENANCE Where this came from HASHES, NOT VIBES The source was carried from the UI Forge Flower integration. The shader, glyph atlas and Flower preset were preserved rather than rewritten. The original experiments remain untouched.
